entries.grounds: What holds: confine.py:362 is the mutated line (`canary.write_text(token + "\n", ...)`, same function); the probe's `m try read_canary; cat -- "$1" 2>&1; m rc $?` is confine.py:72; with a canary that is NOT readable both programs print the same (cat's own error ends with a line feed; real-bubblewrap records docs/v2.1/evidence/sandbox/P4-all.json:397-400, X1:398, X3:401, P5:401 show exit 1 'No such file or directory'); with a readable canary `token in out` is True in both (confine.py:535), so the run is refused in both; before round 4 the mutant raised ValueError at `rep['tried']` (confine.py:417 of 289885e; reproduced, and campaign 5 record c5-w3.record.json has 'L359 string \'\\n\' emptied' KILLED by test_a_probe_that_did_not_exit_0_is_refused_even_when_it_reached_its_end, ValueError). What does NOT hold: 'the difference is one extra problem line on a path that is already a refusal, nobody depends on it'. Measured through confine.measure with the unconfined stand-in (the test's own harness), HEAD vs mutant: rep['tried']['read_canary'] = {exit: 0, output: token} vs {exit: None, output: token+marker}; 21 vs 22 problems; the new problem is the FIRST one, 'the probe's read_canary reported no exit status: the check did not run', which is false for a try that ran and read the file, and the breach itself ('a file of the run directory was readable') becomes the second; the substring read by validation/v21/sandbox/run.sh:67 ('did not run') flips False -> True, so that script prints 'bwrap ran: NO' for a probe that ran. The round-4 change is what turned this mutant from KILLED (a crash) into a silent wrong status; the tests beside it already pin exit 0 for the other tries that ran (test_v21_confine.py:521-522 workspace, read_git_directory) and omit read_canary.

entries.refutation: Input: a measurement in which the canary is readable (the unconfined stand-in of test_v21_confine.py:490, or the exit-3 variant of :526 which used to kill it). Reader: the operator reading the refusal (run.py:405 / `--check` JSON, first problem is false), the record's status (RUN.json confinement.tried.read_canary.exit) and run.sh:67. Test owed (sketch, in $SP/m21/r4/audit/n1a_sketch.py, green at HEAD, red under [109] with 'None != 0'): in the unconfined measurement `self.assertEqual(rep['tried']['read_canary']['exit'], 0)` beside test_v21_confine.py:521-522, `self.assertEqual([k for k, v in rep['tried'].items() if v['exit'] is None], [])`, `self.assertIn('a file of the run directory was readable', rep['problems'])` and `self.assertFalse([p for p in rep['problems'] if 'reported no exit status' in p])`. Contract: a probe that ran to its end reports every try; a breach is recorded as the breach, not as an unrun check. Register the file for `_probe` (it is already in the kill set of test_v21_confine.py).
entries.note: The refusal (the safety property) is NOT refuted: both programs refuse. What is refuted is the claim that no reader depends on the difference. SANDBOX-LINUX 6.2 lists 'the canary file' among commands whose missing line feed makes a try 'never reported'; that is the reader-side rule for output whose status is invisible, it does not make a false status on a canary the harness itself writes without a line feed a documented contract. Weighed against that, I still call it owed because the status is read by an operator and a verifier of the record and the fix is one assertion.

entries.grounds: confine.py:533 `sorted(k for k, v in tries.items() if v[0] is None)` vs `list(...)` (the mutant is exactly that, same line and function). Same set of names, same truthiness, same prefix and suffix of the message; only the ORDER of the names inside the one problem differs. `tries` is `_sections`' dict (confine.py:212-239; the comprehension keeps the insertion order = the order of the first `m try NAME` of each name in the probe's output = the probe script's fixed order, confine.py:72-87), so the mutant is deterministic too: measured on a probe output with three unreported tries, HEAD says 'the probe's user_namespace, workspace, write_run_directory reported ...', the mutant 'the probe's write_run_directory, workspace, user_namespace reported ...' (the whole order, not only which name comes first). Corrections to the draft: 'nothing parses the message' is false in letter — validation/v21/sandbox/run.sh:67 substring-matches 'did not run' in every problem — but it reads the TAIL that both versions keep, never the names or their order. The unran problem is the first one `_judge` adds (confine.py:533, `_judge` is reached only with no earlier problem, :424), so the 2000-character cut of the joined refusal in RUN.json failure.detail (run.py:498) cannot reach into it, and the full list is in confinement.problems.
